decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits close to the core display business and uses existing capacity at low cost, so the firm can carry it with its slack while results are still unclear.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a low-cost variant of the established offer, and nothing indicates a shortfall against aspirations that would trigger search for other uses of the resources.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format that customers routinely demand, so it likely meets the aspiration level.
The eighth-pallet format complements the quarter-pallet range for smaller retail spaces and costs little to keep in the portfolio.
The wooden display pallet strays furthest from the paper-based core and carries more uncertainty, but a large firm's slack allows it more time to prove itself before problemistic search would cut it.
The media-product display serves a niche in declining physical media retail, which raises the risk of a performance shortfall, but it is cheap to maintain within the existing cardboard production.
